Self-Descriptive Sentences

Place ValueNumber TheorySequences
Game: Fill the blanks in a sentence that says how many 0s, 1s, 2s and so on it contains. When the sentence tells the truth, you have found a solution. There is nothing to win — hunt for true sentences.
How to play: Click the left or right half of a blue count to change it, or use arrow keys. Press Iterate, or Auto to keep going; Clear empties the list of past tries.

This sentence contains

Earlier rows

Tap the left half of a count to lower it, the right half to raise it. The counts and the digit labels are written in the chosen base.

Look for the math

Here is a sentence with blanks: "This sentence contains _ 0's, _ 1's, _ 2's, and so on." Can you fill the blanks so that every number is correct?

What gets counted

Write every count in the chosen base, then count how many times each digit appears. The labels 0, 1, 2, ... are part of the sentence too, so every digit gets one free occurrence from its own label. A sentence is true when each count equals one plus the number of times its digit appears in the written counts.

Iterating towards a solution

Start with any counts. Count the digits, write the answers back into the blanks, and repeat. In base three, starting from 1 1 1 gives 1 4 1, then 1 5 1, then 1 4 2 — which is true, because in base three that last line reads 1 11 2. Iterations do not always find a solution: some starting rows fall into cycles, and some true sentences repel the iteration, so no amount of clicking will reach them.

The families of solutions

In base three there are exactly three solutions: 1 11 2, 2 2 10 and 10 10 2. For every base b > 2, the counts 1, 11, 2, 1, 1, ... solve the puzzle, where 11 means b + 1 and the rest are ones. For bases greater than six there is a second family beginning 1, b − 3, 3, 2, .... Try them by hand with the count buttons.

What was checked

The test compares the digit counting with a second transcription of the applet's method, and checks every count row up to 15 in bases two to five. It confirms the three base-three solutions, both solution families in every base the applet offers, and the existence of cycles. The logic test counts 43 separate checks in all.

In base three, set the counts to 0 0 4 and press Auto: the rows repeat instead of settling down.
